review_question: Among patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal lymph nodes, does rapid on-site cytologic evaluation increase the probability of an adequate sample compared with no rapid on-site evaluation?

population.description: Patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes

intervention_or_exposure.description: Rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during sampling

comparator.description: No rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during sampling

targets.comparison: Rapid on-site cytologic evaluation during diagnostic sampling versus no rapid on-site evaluation
targets.population_or_subgroup: Patients undergoing diagnostic sampling of pulmonary lesions or mediastinal or hilar lymph nodes

timepoint_policy.rule: Capture source-defined adequacy assessed during or immediately after the index diagnostic sampling procedure; preserve whether the unit is patient, procedure, or specimen.

candidate_capture_policy.record_scope: Across all known-included reports, capture source-supported arm-level adequate-sampling records after ROSE versus no ROSE and preserve sampling modality and unit of analysis. Do not treat diagnostic yield, sensitivity, accuracy, procedure time, or complication outcomes as adequacy.

targets.quantitative_use_policy: Extract adequate-sample counts and denominators in both groups, the source adequacy definition, sampling modality, analysis unit, and a verified primary-source locator. Do not copy counts or effects from a review forest plot.

output_contract.effect_unit: one source-reported arm-level binary adequate-sampling outcome

target_compatibility.reason: All target families have an existing v1 template.
